paper.title: EgoHumanoid: Unlocking In-the-Wild Loco-Manipulation with Robot-Free Egocentric Demonstration

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct human-to-humanoid data transfer study for real-world loco-manipulation.

sections_read.purpose: Identify the humanoid demonstration scaling problem.
Inspect view and action alignment plus co-training.

sections_read.locator: IV-B Will human data improve humanoid loco-manipulation?

research_question: Can egocentric human demonstrations be aligned with robot data to improve humanoid loco-manipulation generalization?
contributions: View-aligned and action-aligned human/robot co-training for a humanoid whole-body policy.

method.summary: Human egocentric trajectories are transformed into the robot camera/action frame and co-trained with a smaller robot-demonstration anchor set.
assumptions: Human and robot observations can be aligned into a shared egocentric frame.
Some robot demonstrations remain available to anchor embodiment-specific action semantics.

study_context.sample_or_scale: A primary 100-robot plus 300-human training setting with real-world in-domain and generalization evaluation.

evaluation.design: Robot-only and human-robot co-training are compared in-domain and under scene/object generalization; subskill and scaling ablations are included.

findings.finding: Human-robot co-training produced its largest advantage under generalization rather than in-domain evaluation.
findings.scope: The reported tasks and one humanoid platform.
findings.locator: IV-B Will human data improve humanoid loco-manipulation?

author_stated.limitation: Orientation alignment remains ambiguous, data demand exceeds fixed-base manipulation, and the study uses one platform.

reader_inferred.boundary: Human data transfers navigation and coarse reaching more readily than precision manipulation.
reader_inferred.basis: The subskill analysis reports stronger transfer for locomotion than contact-sensitive manipulation, and robot anchors remain necessary.

transfer_boundary: Most credible for visually aligned, egocentric skills with shared scene semantics and a robot-data anchor set.

design_risks: Task scoring and platform choice may shape the magnitude of gains.
Human and robot dataset size are jointly changed in some conditions.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Robot-only and co-trained policies share the same robot data; co-training receives additional human data by design.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task and subskill scores reveal where cross-embodiment transfer helps.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Alignment and data protocols are described with appendices.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: One robot and a bounded task family.

evidence_cards.claim: With 100 robot and 300 human demonstrations, co-training scored 78% versus 59% for robot-only in-domain, and 82% versus 31% under generalization.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports aligned human data as a generalization prior for humanoid loco-manipulation.
evidence_cards.summary: The main comparison directly reports both in-domain and generalization gaps.
evidence_cards.locator: IV-B Will human data improve humanoid loco-manipulation?
evidence_cards.source_context: For in-domain evaluation, co-training achieves 78% average score versus 59% for robot-only. The gap widens remarkably in generalization settings: co-training reaches 82% compared to 31% for robot-only.

quantitative.locator: IV-B Will human data improve humanoid loco-manipulation?

verification.rationale: The result text explicitly states the two settings, both systems and all four values.
